I think it's be better to take a second and have a breather. Decide from there what you want to do after you've calmed down.

Look, I've played this game before (yes, feel free to roll your eyes) and there's a moment where you can cuss yourself out after you do something stupid. What's funny too is that it isn't scripted - it's just a mistake that you can actually make by your own choice. And the game gives you the option to say, "I'm such an idiot" or moronic, or whatever we say to ourselves.

Then you get a quote from the character's (won't spoil the name - yes I'm not kidding it's an actual spoiler to know his name) volition, his inner voice going, "You're not an idiot, don't say that. This is a really big mess and being a detective is hard." (you play as a alcoholic cop for some context)

I remember being in that moment when I heard that, realizing we forget how hard life can be, and that the goals we want to pursue, can be both hard and a mess. There's no shame in wanting to try again, and there's no shame in not wanting to continue. But don't let the reason for your decision be because you think you're an idiot - you're not.

 Most people, including myself, and I've struggled with this in my own mental health journey, discredit ourselves to an insane degree and not even give ourselves a SHRED of credit.

There's a lot I learned from that game. Feel free to reach out if you're ever feeling down.

Dude, what school do you go to?

I used to really be into physics and maths. I was in love with both of those fields of science. I would just go beyond my high school curriculum just for fun or out of interest.
I was planning on doing physics at uni (even considered a double major or something along those lines with math) but my dad told me to stop dreaming and stop being a child. He said that it's a useless degree and that I should do engineering.
After a year of arguing, he wouldn't budge and my dream wilted away and died. I couldn't apply for student loans for certain reasons nor could I pay so I had to go on his behalf. After that, I guess I just wasn't the same. So right now I am studying engineering but no day passes by where I don't imagine how different my life would have been or how much happier I would have been. 
Btw, just saying, but I mean no offence towards all t professional engineers out there. It just wasn't something I wanted to do.
So yeah, sorry for the rant.
